decisions.context: Each transaction needs a score before authorization, so the application needs an online model interface. The design space includes service-based and in-application integration patterns (d:1).
decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides the choice: a separately scalable service isolates scoring capacity, at the cost of a network hop that must fit the latency budget.
consequences: Keep the synchronous request path within the latency budget.

decisions.context: The authorization flow needs a transaction score in real time, making online serving necessary (d:5).
decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides the choice: distributed serving can scale for transaction peaks; the cost is remote-call overhead against the latency target.
consequences: Provision and scale serving capacity for peaks.
Measure request latency across the network boundary.

decisions.decision: How to ingest and process transaction data?
decisions.context: Fraud scoring occurs on each transaction, so fresh data must be available on the online path (d:7, d:15).

alternatives.label: Streamed ingestion with real-time processing
cons: Peak availability: stream processing adds operational load

alternatives.label: Batch ingestion with batch processing
pros: Peak availability: process off the request path

decisions.rationale: Tens-of-ms scoring on current transactions decides the choice: streaming keeps inputs fresh, at the cost of additional processing operations. The selected point pairs streamed ingestion with real-time processing (v:15.2).
consequences: Keep feature computation off the critical scoring path where possible.

decisions.decision: How to persist and provide access to features?
decisions.context: The scorer needs transaction features during the online request, and auditors need to know which features contributed to a score (d:4, d:22).

alternatives.label: Feature store
cons: Audit traceability: requires recorded feature references

alternatives.label: Store features in data stores without specific support
cons: Latency: access may vary across stores

decisions.rationale: Tens-of-ms latency decides the choice: a feature store gives the serving path a focused feature access pattern; it still requires recording the feature values or references for each score.
consequences: Design online feature access for the latency budget.
Capture the features used with each scored transaction.

decisions.decision: How to track model versions and scoring inputs?
decisions.context: Auditors must be able to reconstruct which model version and features produced a score, so production records must link predictions to their inputs and model identity (d:22).

alternatives.label: Model in-production tracking
pros: Audit traceability: tracks inputs and outputs
cons: Latency: recording adds work to the request path

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
pros: Audit traceability: records data and predictions
cons: Reproducibility: may omit model usage details

decisions.rationale: Audit traceability decides the choice: the design space describes tracking inputs, outputs, and model usage; recording this context costs storage and processing.
consequences: Retain model identity and scoring inputs with each prediction.
Set retention and access rules for audit records.

decisions.decision: How to manage model versions in production?
decisions.context: Auditors need the model version for every score, and production must remain available while versions change (d:10).

alternatives.label: Single model in production
cons: Peak availability: rollout may require a switch

alternatives.label: N versions in production
cons: Audit traceability: route and record version per score

decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides the choice: rollback provides a recovery path after a bad release; preserving the version-to-score history adds operational recordkeeping.
consequences: Maintain a deployable previous model version.
Record the active model version for each score.

decisions.context: Reproducing an audited score depends on identifying the data and features used during model development and production (d:11).

alternatives.label: Data versioning in code repository
cons: Audit traceability: large data handling may be constrained

alternatives.label: No data versioning
cons: Reproducibility: inputs may not be recoverable

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice: explicit data versions support repeatable model builds; operating a separate repository adds management cost.
consequences: Keep data versions linked to model releases.
Retain the feature inputs or references needed to reconstruct a score.
